title: Counterexamples to two conjectures on modular edge colorings of graphs
summary: For an integer $k\geq2$, let $χ_k'(G)$ denote the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of a graph $G$ such that every nonzero degree in each color subgraph is congruent to $1\pmod{k}$. A graph is a $0_k$-graph if every vertex degree is divisible by $k$. We disprove a conjecture of Berthe et al.\ (On modular edge colorings of graphs, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40 (2026) 897--904), which states that $χ_k'(G)\leq k+o(k)$ for every $0_k$-graph $G$.
